cohort: The study included 50 pregnant women, divided into a control group of 25 normotensive women and a study group of 25 age- and sex-matched preeclamptic women, with samples collected immediately after delivery.
finding: Preeclamptic women exhibited significantly elevated maternal and cord blood heme oxygenase-1 levels and significantly lower endoglin levels compared to normotensive women, leading to a drastically doubled HO-1/Endoglin ratio.
